title: Risk Scoring Now Vetoes Serial Token Scammers | vitalii.no
description:
The risk scorer only looked at top-10 holder concentration and a couple of source flags, so a wallet that had already minted dozens of throwaway tokens, or a coin nobody was actually net-buying, could pass with the same score as a clean one — the data that would catch a serial scammer or a dead-on-arrival launch just wasn't being fetched.

src/lib/jupiter.ts now pulls Jupiter's Tokens v2 API (stats5m/stats1h, holderCount, and an audit block with devMints, devBalancePercentage, topHoldersPercentage) as the primary market-data source, replacing DexScreener as the main feed and falling back to it only for mints Jupiter misses or for socials. scoreCandidate() reads the new dev_mints, net_buyers, holders and traders columns: dev_mints over 50 is a hard veto, over 10 costs 15 points; net_buyers at or below zero costs 12 points; fewer than 20 holders costs 10 points; fewer than 10 traders costs 8 points. The scan limit also went from 85 to 180 mints per cycle now that Jupiter batches up to 100 mints per request.

A wallet with a track record of mass-minting tokens is now vetoed outright instead of scoring the same as a first-time launch, and coins with no real net buyers or too few holders lose points before the AI ever sees them.
